title: The tame Galois sequence of a henselian discrete valuation field
statement:
Let $R$ be an excellent discrete valuation ring [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] which is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], with algebraically closed residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, choose a separable closure $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and equip $G=\operatorname{Gal}(F^{\mathrm{sep}}/F)$ with its profinite Krull topology. There is a closed normal subgroup $P$ and a continuous surjective homomorphism
$$
\theta:G\longrightarrow\prod_{r\text{ prime},\ r\neq p}(\mathbf Z_r,+)
$$
with kernel $P$, inducing an isomorphism of topological groups $G/P\cong\prod_{r\neq p}(\mathbf Z_r,+)$. Every finite continuous quotient of $P$ has order a power of $p$. Here $\mathbf Z_r$ denotes the $r$-adic integers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], with inverse-limit topology $\mathbf Z_r=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\mathbf Z/r^n\mathbf Z$, and the displayed product has its product topology. The map $\theta$ may depend on choices of compatible roots of unity; no canonical trivialization of a Tate twist is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0BUB, lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure; specialization to a henselian DVR with algebraically closed residue field, with compatible roots of unity and the Chinese remainder decomposition of the tame inverse limit

proof.text: Because the residue field is algebraically closed, R is strictly henselian. Apply [lem-per-trait-tame-algebra] with the algebraic closure of the chosen separable closure as its coefficient field. The residue characteristic exponent is p since p is prime and CharP(k,p). Retain its continuous surjective tame character t and its finite continuous quotient assertion for ker(t), and its compatible primitive-root family in the coefficient field.

Choose a compatible primitive-root family in k by [lem-exc-tame-roots-product]. For each positive m prime to p identify the m-th root groups in the two fields by sending the a-th power of the first primitive root to the a-th power of the second. Mathlib IsPrimitiveRoot.zmodEquivZPowers gives these finite group equivalences. Compatibility of the chosen roots makes the equivalences commute with the power transitions: write an arbitrary coordinate as a power of the primitive root and commute the two exponents. Apply the equivalences coordinatewise to root-limit families. The reverse coordinate equivalences are inverse, and both maps are continuous because each output coordinate depends only on its corresponding discrete input coordinate. This constructs a topological group equivalence b between the two root limits, without any field map between the coefficient field and k.

Compose b with the residue-field root-limit equivalence c of [lem-exc-tame-roots-product], and put theta=(c composed with b) composed with t. It is continuous and surjective. Injectivity of c composed with b gives ker(theta)=ker(t). The product of the adic integers is Hausdorff; therefore this kernel P is closed. As the kernel of a homomorphism it is normal. The finite continuous quotients of P have p-power order by the assertion retained in Step 1.

The first isomorphism theorem and ker(theta)=P give an algebraic equivalence G/P to the adic product, agreeing with theta on every quotient representative. The quotient-map universal property makes it continuous. The Krull Galois group is compact, hence its quotient is compact, and the adic product is Hausdorff. A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism. This supplies exactly the required continuous multiplicative equivalence and its projection identity.
